data.narrative: The student implemented core API and redirect behavior with strong security boundaries, then validated both success and failure paths with reproducible evidence. During BREAK/FIX, they diagnosed route-contract drift quickly and restored the namespaced redirect route without collateral regressions. Their decisions consistently balanced security, reliability, and maintainability.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose namespaced redirect routing to reduce collisions while preserving public redirect usability.
dimension_scores.evidence: Decision reasoning explicitly favored /r/{code} to avoid conflicts with /health, /ready, and /links while supporting future route growth.

dimension_scores.observation: Applied hypothesis-driven diagnosis from symptom to route-map confirmation and repair.
dimension_scores.evidence: Observed /r/{code} 404, proposed route-registration hypothesis, checked OpenAPI, confirmed registered path drift to /{code}, restored /r/{code}, and re-verified redirect plus health.

dimension_scores.observation: Implemented explicit scheme allowlist and reasoned about phishing-abuse beyond basic validation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Accepted https URL, rejected javascript variants with 400, and identified residual risk of phishing on valid http/https with mitigation via reputation and abuse controls.

dimension_scores.observation: Protected route contracts and verified non-regression after fix with targeted checks.
dimension_scores.evidence: Verified 307 redirect with correct Location and /health 200 after route fix, showing both functional recovery and operational safety.

dimension_scores.observation: Communicated concise, technically precise explanations tied to exact outputs and failure modes.
dimension_scores.evidence: Consistently reported status/body/header details and articulated boundary rationale for 400 vs 500 and 410 behavior for expired links.

strengths: Strong security boundary design at both input and routing layers.
Fast, evidence-driven root-cause isolation during route regression.
Consistent use of reproducible command/output proof for progression.
data.recommendation: In Module 4, keep the same rigor by adding automated route-contract tests (including /r/{code}, /health, and auth-protected paths) to catch boundary regressions before release.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented and verified create-link behavior with input validation.
public_evidence.technical_detail: POST /links validates URL schemes with an allowlist boundary before business logic/persistence.
public_evidence.proof: Valid create returned 200 with short_code and long_url; malicious javascript payload returned 400 with validation error.
public_evidence.ability: Builds secure input boundaries for public-facing APIs.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows ability to prevent unsafe input ingestion while preserving expected user flows.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented and restored namespaced redirect behavior with route-safety verification.
public_evidence.technical_detail: GET /r/{code} route used as isolated public redirect namespace to avoid collisions with service/admin endpoints.
public_evidence.proof: GET /r/abc123 returned 307 Temporary Redirect with Location: https://example.com and /health remained 200 after route changes.
public_evidence.ability: Designs and validates stable public routing contracts.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates production routing discipline and non-regression verification under change.

public_evidence.student_action: Diagnosed /r/{code} failure and localized root cause to route-map drift.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Used OpenAPI route inspection to confirm path changed from /r/{code} to /{code}, then restored intended contract.
public_evidence.proof: OpenAPI output showed /{code} during failure; after fix, redirect verification succeeded with expected status and header.
public_evidence.ability: Performs focused incident triage and contract restoration.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows practical debugging maturity for API regressions in live-like conditions.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Explained why /r/{code} separates redirect traffic from admin/health routes and reduces collisions.
Explained 400 for invalid client URL input and why 500 would misclassify failure.
Provided 307 and Location-header proof for redirect correctness.

concepts_demonstrated.concept: Residual abuse risk after scheme validation
concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Identified phishing risk on valid http/https and proposed layered mitigation.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used concrete request/response evidence to anchor security and HTTP-behavior reasoning.
Required hypothesis-first diagnosis and exact verification outputs before progression.
